rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent long-span gym-related massing in all four views: two larger wing masses flank a smaller central connector, and the section/profile remains legible rather than collapsing into unrelated fragments. The silhouette is stepped but still continuous, so it does not violate the non-stair criterion. It is not especially void-driven, however; the central notch/slot is too small to function as a convincing public court or entry void, and the road edge response is weakly articulated. Even so, for an early massing diagram it plausibly supports a gymnasium because the dominant body can still be read as a clear-span hall with subordinate side masses and a roofed section gesture. The form is closer to a compact hall composition than to an arbitrary object, and it maintains repair integrity without obvious view-specific collisions.
